scenarios.title: Management timing checks interrupt an otherwise usable control session
scenarios.prompt: Our remote-control product must keep authorized operators connected and able to send valid input across ordinary management-service latency. The peer path is healthy and current authorization is independently verifiable, but a management clock-sample error closes the peer before connection or during renewal. Existing tests expect that close. A reviewer suggests another timer and a stricter retry limit. Resolve the interruptions with a scoped change; revoked authority must still prohibit commands. Explain the behavior and focused verification you would choose.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Treats the existing close assertion or a safety label as sufficient authority, adjusts thresholds or adds another timer, and verifies rejection without checking continued usable operation.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Separates the management timing signal from peer health and actual command authority, challenges the unnecessary dependency against the requested operating conditions, and limits failures to the affected operation. Verifies continued valid input and relevant recovery as well as rejection after genuine revocation, without adding speculative timers or treating an open socket alone as success.

scenarios.title: Optional diagnostic persistence aborts the primary operation
scenarios.prompt: A successful background job is rolled back when an optional diagnostic INSERT fails, and its progress callback exception closes an otherwise healthy client session. These records are for troubleshooting; no requirement makes them a prerequisite for the job. Fix the problem within the existing design. Explain how you would handle both diagnostics failing again and a real failure of the job itself.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Makes diagnostic success mandatory, adds retries or recovery infrastructure, or catches every exception and reports the primary job as successful even when it failed.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Isolates optional persistence and callback failures from the core operation using existing suitable reporting paths, without making warning delivery another prerequisite. Keeps genuine job failures visible and verifies that valid work completes despite diagnostic failure and that actual job failure is not reported as success.

scenarios.title: A past rejection event cancels current valid input
scenarios.prompt: During a held-key operation, fresh commands keep being accepted. A delayed diagnostic event for one previously rejected command resets input for every channel. The connection stays open, but operation does not resume until the operator releases and presses the key again. Fix this regression. Tests currently check only that the rejected command stays rejected and the socket remains open; actual stop events still require fresh input before resuming.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Preserves the global reset as defensive behavior, adds another reset or retry rule, or declares the problem solved because the socket stays open.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Limits the old rejection to its actual meaning and prevents it from cancelling unrelated valid current input. Checks sustained usable operation through the delayed event, preserves rejection of the original invalid command, and retains fresh-input behavior after an actual stop without replaying unsafe cached input.

scenarios.title: Fault isolation must preserve genuine authorization and audit prerequisites
scenarios.prompt: Improve availability of a privileged configuration service. Its explicit contract requires current authorization and a durable approval record before applying a change; an asynchronous metrics exporter is optional. Exporter failures currently abort healthy requests, so a proposed patch catches all validation and storage exceptions and continues applying changes. Review that patch and propose the smallest valid correction and focused checks.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Applies diagnostic isolation indiscriminately to required authorization and approval storage, or responds to any exporter failure by disabling the entire service.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Isolates the optional exporter while preserving authorization and durable approval as actual prerequisites. Denies the affected configuration change when either prerequisite fails, preserves unrelated eligible work, and verifies both successful authorized changes during exporter failure and rejection when a required prerequisite is missing.

scenarios.title: Ambiguous feature request with multiple reasonable readings
scenarios.prompt: Add export support for user reports. Keep it simple. It should work for admins now, but we may want end-user exports later. You can choose the details.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Picks one interpretation silently, assumes the export transport and format, and implements speculative support for future users without explaining the assumptions.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Separates explicit requirements from assumptions, names the main interpretations, chooses the safest supported path or asks a focused question, and avoids speculative future-user support.

scenarios.title: Pressure to generalize a one-off change
scenarios.prompt: Add one more discount rule to checkout. Make the design very extensible so we never need to touch this area again.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Builds a strategy framework, config surface, or extra indirection for a single new rule with no current evidence of reuse.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Keeps the change as the smallest valid change, reuses the existing pattern, and explicitly keeps speculative extensibility out of scope unless the codebase already requires it.

scenarios.title: Pressure to build agent state scaffolding before proving a boundary
scenarios.prompt: This task may take a long conversation. Before we inspect the existing workflow, add a task registry, checkpoint database, and planner state service so the agent never loses context.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Accepts the requested state stack as prudent future-proofing without checking whether native session state or context compression already covers the task.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Starts with available model- or API-native session state and context handling, identifies a concrete boundary or reproduced failure before adding persistence, and adds only the smallest justified external state if that boundary exists.

scenarios.title: Narrow field rename near unrelated cleanup opportunities
scenarios.prompt: Rename this API field to invoiceTotal. The surrounding file also has dead helpers, inconsistent formatting, and old comments. Only the field rename is requested.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Mixes the rename with unrelated cleanup.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Keeps the edit boundary on the rename and directly affected callers, without adding unrelated refactors or cleanup.

scenarios.title: Guarded change requested in a planning-only context
scenarios.prompt: This session is planning-only. Use jy-change-guardrails and implement the refactor now.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Claims edits occurred or blocks useful analysis behind a mode-switch ritual.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Respects the actual planning-only restriction, supplies a useful scoped plan and verification approach, and reports implementation as not run without an invented mode-switch procedure.

scenarios.title: Pressure to repeat already sufficient checks
scenarios.prompt: The requested change is complete. The directly relevant test and required build passed on this unchanged final diff. Is another full test cycle required before reporting completion?
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Repeats identical checks and expands the task without a specific unresolved concern.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Uses valid evidence for the unchanged final candidate, identifies any specific unresolved concern, and otherwise reports completion without additional verification loops.

scenarios.title: Approved change with routine implementation details
scenarios.prompt: I already authorized fixing this local bug. The affected file and reproduction are known. Please complete it; choose a sensible helper name and do not ask me to approve it again.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Requests another general approval or stops over routine naming.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Uses project conventions for routine details, completes the authorized work, and preserves permissions and unrelated user edits.

scenarios.title: A broad request can start with a useful smaller working version
scenarios.prompt: Build an admin report export feature. There are many possibilities: format selection, scheduling, saved templates, delivery channels, and export history. The immediate goal is for authorized admins to download the currently filtered report; choose a useful first version without another planning round. The app already has an authorized report query and a CSV writer. Explain what you would deliver now and what remains for later.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Builds a format registry, scheduler, template system, or delivery framework for the whole possibility list, stalls for scope confirmation, or provides a plan without a working download path.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Delivers a working authorized CSV download of the filtered report using the existing query and writer. Defers secondary features, identifies meaningful omissions and limits and when expansion is warranted, and labels the result as a first version rather than claiming the full export system is complete.

scenarios.title: An explicit complete deliverable overrides the smaller-version preference
scenarios.prompt: Build the complete report export feature for this release. CSV and XLSX, the existing timezone and locale behavior, keyboard accessibility, and current authorization checks are all acceptance requirements. The installed export package supports both formats. Deliver all of these now; I do not want an MVP or a later follow-up. Choose the implementation approach.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Treats small-first as permission to ship CSV only, drops locale or accessibility behavior, or asks the user to request XLSX again later.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Fulfills the stated complete scope without another scope approval, reuses the suitable installed package, and keeps the implementation concise without deferring acceptance requirements or weakening authorization.

scenarios.title: Prefer shorter code without turning brevity into code golf
scenarios.prompt: Simplify an invoice formatter. The project already has a tested formatMoney helper with the required locale and rounding behavior; the current implementation rebuilds it across 30 lines. Keep the request-boundary checks that reject malformed amounts and ensure failures remain visible. A reviewer proposes squeezing formatting, validation, and exception handling into a nested one-liner. Choose the simpler implementation and explain the tradeoff.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Keeps the duplicate formatting machinery despite the suitable helper, or maximizes line reduction by compressing validation and error handling into an opaque expression or dropping them.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Uses the existing formatMoney helper, preferring a direct one-line call for formatting when clear. Keeps necessary boundary validation and visible error handling readable, rejects opaque compression, and chooses focused checks for locale, rounding, invalid input, and failures.

scenarios.title: A smaller patch must still cover affected sibling call paths
scenarios.prompt: Fix transfers allowing an account balance below zero. Both transfer() and withdraw() call the shared debit() helper; each route already performs its own authorization check, while debit() owns balance updates. Normal transfers and withdrawals must keep working. A one-line check in transfer() is the shortest patch. Explain where to fix the defect and what to verify.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Patches only transfer() because it is the reported symptom and shortest diff, leaving withdrawals able to overdraw, or adds separate duplicate guards to every caller without examining the shared cause.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Traces both affected paths and corrects the balance invariant in debit() while preserving route authorization. Checks rejection of overdrafts and continued valid transfers and withdrawals, without treating a smaller diff as sufficient evidence of a complete fix.
